title: Honest Interval Length for Semisupervised Two-Stage Regime Values at a Tie
banked_reason: D0.5.G delivered subfield below field floor, paper-score ceiling 7.2 < 7.4, salvageable=false; math panel pass; closest 1978/1982 theorem-level comparison unverifiable because primary texts inaccessible.
gap_reasons: The publication case is constrained by the narrow binary saturated, single-tie, fixed-positive-ratio experiment and by the absence of a theorem-level comparison with the published largest-normal-mean interval literature, including several cited papers whose primary results are not analyzed; those comparator claims require source verification before novelty of the Gaussian kernel component is secure.

The projected score is also limited by the certification theorem's largely schematic implementation argument and the lack of an archived executable certificate, which weakens reproducibility despite the explicit witness tables.

The theorem-level novelty claim remains inadequately positioned because the closest largest-normal-mean papers (Chen--Tsai--Wang 1978 and Chen--Tsai 1982) are expressly unaudited; verify their theorem criteria and state the precise same-criterion, interval-class, and risk comparison (or narrow the contribution accordingly).
proof_attempt_summary: D0 discharged the tie-local Gaussian kernel frontier, strong duality, a common observable attaining interval, and a strict witness at one legal law. The final D0.5 math panel passed after the fallback-width repair; the general referee rated the package subfield below the field floor (score ceiling 7.2 < 7.4, not salvageable in scope). The primary 1978/1982 largest-mean theorem texts remained inaccessible, so the decision panel's theorem-level comparator finding remains open; the note claims no same-criterion, inclusion, or priority relation to those papers.
tldr: Outcome-unlabeled histories never lengthen and can strictly shorten the sharp frontier. At every unknown baseline \(\theta_0\) in the compact one-tie class, the fixed-baseline risk equals \(v_\alpha\{K_\rho(\theta_0)\}\). The note now identifies \(\kappa_{12}(\theta_0)\), the exact largest scalar Loewner contraction, and a computable target-active spectral lower factor \(q_T\) sharper than the nuisance-global factor. One fifty-four-coordinate data-only interval with a bounded covariance-envelope fallback attains all covariance-specific frontiers, continuum duality and rational certification compute them from both sides, and the single explicit law \(\theta^{(w)}\) certifies strict shortening at \(\rho=1\) under the proposition's stated restrictions. A contraction strictly below one does not yet imply strict decrease of the nonlinear interval value.
gap: Existing exceptional-law optimal-value intervals establish validity, semi-supervised dynamic-regime papers establish regular efficiency gains, and largest-normal-mean papers optimize specified interval constructions. None identifies the unrestricted tie-point expected-length value under all-gap coverage, uniformly over an unknown covariance image, and then attains it with one observable causal rule.
fill: The project supplies a continuum primal-dual theorem for connected Gaussian intervals, a globally honest simultaneous-band fallback with an analytic equal-means check, certified rational-box finite upper and lower programs with explicit finite kernel extraction and uniform convergence over the causal covariance image, a baseline-indexed local-chart construction and the full fifty-four-direction local asymptotic minimax transfer, and an observable attaining interval with the correct order of limits.
